sections.h2: What should a Mount Juliet seller expect?
sections.html:
Mount Juliet is the largest city in Wilson County, about 17 miles east of downtown Nashville, and its housing numbers look more like a commuter suburb than a small town. Census data put the median value of owner-occupied homes at $460,100 and the owner-occupied rate at 72.1 percent. With larger dollar amounts at stake, small items such as a roof, an HVAC unit or a tax bill have a bigger effect on the check you take away.

The Census Bureau estimates 45,172 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 39,289 at the 2020 census. Earlier census counts were 2,879 in 1980, 12,366 in 2000 and 23,671 in 2010, so the city has multiplied several times over in a generation.

sections.h2: Where is Mount Juliet and how did it develop?
sections.html:
The city lies mostly between Interstate 40 and U.S. Route 70, with Old Hickory Lake to the north and Percy Priest Lake to the south. State Route 171, also called Mt. Juliet Road, links US 70 to I-40, which has two exits in the city. Nashville International Airport is about 9 miles west, and the WeGo Star commuter train stops in Mount Juliet on its Nashville to Lebanon run.

The settlement dates to 1835, the city incorporated in 1972, and it is named for the Mount Juliet Estate in County Kilkenny, Ireland. It is the only city in the country with that name. City government is a commission and city manager system, with a mayor and four district commissioners. The city runs its own police department and a career fire department with three stations.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Mount Juliet homes?
sections.html:
Wilson County Schools operates the public schools. Elementary schools serving the city include Springdale, Mt. Juliet, Elzie D. Patton, W. A. Wright, Lakeview and Rutland. Middle schools include Mt. Juliet Middle, West Wilson Middle and Gladeville Middle. Most of the city is zoned to Mt. Juliet High School, the northwestern part to Green Hill High School, and the area south of I-40 to Wilson Central High School.

Zoning follows the address, so a buyer may ask which high school your street feeds. Check with Wilson County Schools before you answer, because zoning can change.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 tornado change for Mount Juliet homes?
sections.html:
In the early morning of March 3, 2020, an EF3 tornado destroyed hundreds of Mount Juliet homes, along with West Wilson Middle School and Stoner Creek Elementary. Five people died across the storm's path, three of them in Mount Juliet.

  • If your house was damaged and repaired, keep permits, inspection sign-offs and contractor invoices.
  • Note the age of the roof and when it was last replaced.
  • Keep any insurance claim paperwork from storm damage.

Handing a buyer this file up front shortens the back and forth after an offer.

sections.h2: How does property tax work in Mount Juliet?
sections.html:
Mount Juliet property owners pay two bills. The city bill goes to the City of Mt. Juliet, and the county bill goes to the Wilson County Trustee. The City Board of Commissioners approved a city rate of 28 cents per $100 of assessed value for the budget year that began July 1, 2026, and the city calls this the lowest municipal rate in Wilson County. After the county's recent reappraisal, the certified county rate is $1.1657 per $100.

  • Taxes are payable October 1 and become delinquent March 1 of the following year.
  • You can pay without penalty or interest through the last day of February.
  • To claim the deduction on the same year's federal return, pay by December 31.
  • Notices go to the owner of record as of January 1, and the city also sends information to mortgage servicers that request it.

If you do not receive a notice by the end of October from both the city and the county, contact each office. Mailing address changes can only be made through the Wilson County Property Assessor, 228 East Main Street, Room 4, Lebanon, at 615-444-8661. The City Finance office is at 2425 North Mt. Juliet Road, 615-773-6208, and the Trustee is in Room 102 of the courthouse at 615-444-0894.

sections.h2: What permits does a Mount Juliet seller need for repairs?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department, at 115 Clemmons Road, enforces building, electrical and plumbing codes under the 2018 International Codes and the 2017 National Electrical Code. Permit hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, the phone is 615-773-6225, and next-day inspection requests have to arrive by 2 p.m. at bldg@mtjuliet-tn.gov.

An owner must get a permit before constructing, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a building, adding a pool, deck, arbor or storage building, or changing electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems. The department lists exceptions, including fences not over 7 feet, retaining walls not over 4 feet, and prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep. If you are unsure whether a repair needs a permit, ask before the work starts, because open permits can slow a closing.

sections.h2: What should a Mount Juliet seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
Two tax bills and a county recording office mean a few details are easy to miss. Work through this list with your title company:

  • Ask the City Finance office for the city balance and the Wilson County Trustee for the county balance on your parcel.
  • Confirm whether the October bill has already been issued, since notices are mailed each October.
  • Collect permit records for any work done since you bought, and ask Building and Codes about any open permit.
  • Pull your deed from the Register of Deeds so the legal description matches the contract.
  • Give the buyer your mortgage servicer's name so the payoff letter can be ordered early.

The title company will prorate taxes between you and the buyer, and the county Trustee can confirm what has been paid for the current year.

sections.h2: Where do Mount Juliet deeds get recorded?
sections.html: Wilson County keeps its Register of Deeds in the Wilson County Courthouse in Lebanon, the same building that houses the Property Assessor and the Trustee. The state's recordation tax on the transfer is $0.37 per $100, based on the greater of the price or the value, and the buyer as grantee pays it. The register collects it before recording. Call the Register's office for its current recording fees before closing.

faqs.q: What is the Mount Juliet city property tax rate?
faqs.a: 28 cents per $100 of assessed value, set by the Board of Commissioners for the budget year starting July 1, 2026. The county adds its own rate, certified at $1.1657 per $100 after the latest reappraisal.

faqs.q: When do Mount Juliet property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. Bills are payable October 1, and the city says you can pay without penalty or interest through the last day of February. Pay by December 31 if you want the federal deduction for that year.

faqs.q: Who do I tell when my mailing address changes in Mount Juliet?
faqs.a: Only the Wilson County Property Assessor, at 615-444-8661. Neither the city nor the county Trustee can change a mailing address on the tax roll.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a fence in Mount Juliet?
faqs.a: Not for a fence 7 feet tall or lower, which is one of the listed exceptions. Anything taller, and work such as electrical, plumbing or additions, needs a permit from the Building and Codes Department.

faqs.q: What did the 2020 tornado do to Mount Juliet?
faqs.a: An EF3 tornado on March 3, 2020 destroyed hundreds of homes plus West Wilson Middle School and Stoner Creek Elementary. Five people were killed, three of them in Mount Juliet.
